summary: Adolf Kirchhoff was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh. He taught at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium and held professorships at Humboldt University and Frederick William University Berlin.

Adolphe Regnier worked in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology, having studied under Eugène Burnouf. His appointments included positions at the Collège de France, École Normale Supérieure (1841–1843), Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (1855), and Palace of Fontainebleau (1873).

Adrian Zenz specializes in Tibetology and Sinology. He studied at the University of Auckland and the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger. He later held posts at the European School of Culture and Theology and the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation.

Agata Bareja-Starzyńska is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She conducted research at the University of Oslo (1993) and the University of Bonn (1995), and held an attested post at the University of Warsaw in 2008.

Agathon Benary worked in linguistics. He studied at the universities of Göttingen and Halle-Wittenberg, and under Franz Bopp. Benary served as a gymnasial teacher at Köllnisches Gymnasium (1833–1860) and as a Privatdozent at Humboldt University of Berlin (1839).

Agehananda Bharati specialized in religious studies and Indology, studying at the University of Vienna. He held teaching posts at several institutions in India and Japan before serving as Ford-Maxwell Professor of South Asian Studies at Syracuse University (1961–1991).

Agnieszka Helman-Ważny specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at the Academy of Fine Arts in Warsaw and Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń. She held an affiliation at Cornell University (attested 2009) and a post at the University of Warsaw (2015).

Agvan Dorzhiev was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery and Drepung Gomang Dratsang, earning the Geshe Lharampa degree. He founded Atsagat Datsan and Datsan Gunzechoinei, and his students included the 13th Dalai Lama.

Ahmad Hasan Dani was a scholar in archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of London under Mortimer Wheeler, Kenneth de Burgh Codrington, and A. S. Altekar, holding posts at Dhaka, Peshawar, and Quaid-i-Azam universities.

Aiko Okoshi was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. She completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University from ~1970 to 1975 and was appointed a full-time lecturer at Kindai University in 1990.

Ajahn Amaro is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Bedford College, London, and trained under Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho. He served as co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery (~1996–2010) and became abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery in ~2010.

Ajahn Brahm is a Buddhist and religious studies teacher. He studied at the University of Cambridge and trained under Boonman Poonsuwan and Ajahn Chah. He has served as the abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery since ~1983.

Ajahn Maha Somchai Kusalacitto works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Madras and served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, attested in 2003.
Ajahn Pasanno is a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who trained under Ajahn Chah from ~1974 to 1982. He served as founding co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery from ~1996 to 2018.
Ajahn Sucitto is a Buddhist studies figure who earned a degree from the University of Warwick. He studied under Ajahn Sumedho beginning in 1977 and served as abbot of Cittaviveka from 1992 to 2014.

Ajahn Sumedho is a Buddhist studies teacher who earned a master's degree from the University of California, Berkeley and trained under Ajahn Chah. He served as abbot of Wat Pa Nanachat (1975) and Amaravati Buddhist Monastery (1984–2010).
Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya. He held a position at the University of Calcutta as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow.

Akifumi Naito specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University, Honganji Sōgakuin, and under Gadjin M. Nagao. He held posts at Ryukoku University, Jodo Shinshu Institute, Kyoto Women's University, and Gyoshin Buddhist Academy.

Akihiko Akamatsu is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Paris under Yuichi Kajiyama. He held faculty posts at Kyushu University and Kyoto University, where he later served as trustee and vice-president.

Akihiro Oda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University. He held academic appointments there as a full-time lecturer (attested 1992) and later as Professor of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013).
